prompt:
## Deliverable
Normalise the single contact record in the user message. Return exactly one bare JSON object with exactly five keys: name, phone, email, company, country. Every value is a string or JSON null. No prose, fences, extra keys or questions.

## Read the whole record, then assign fields
The record is a block of label–value lines within a note. Recognise label variants and colon, equals or tab separators in any order. Ignore all surrounding notes and signatures. Trim each value and collapse internal whitespace runs to one space. Absent and empty values and the following placeholders, in any case, are null: -, --, n/a, na, none, unknown, ?, null, TBD.

Look across the record, not just at the corresponding labels. A value containing @ is the email. A value with at least seven digits and no characters other than digits, spaces and + - ( ) . / after removing a leading tel: and an extension is the phone. Strip phone extensions written as ext. plus digits, ext plus digits, x plus digits, # plus digits, or extension plus digits. Name and company come from their respective lines unless the name-labelled value ends in a legal suffix from the list below and the company-labelled value does not: in that case swap the two values. Only the country line supplies explicit country.

## Resolve the country and phone together
Convert the explicit country to uppercase ISO 3166-1 alpha-2. Recognise English, Swedish and German names, alpha-2 and alpha-3 codes, and common aliases case-insensitively. UK and Great Britain → GB; Holland → NL; USA and U.S.A. → US; Türkiye → TR; Czech Republic → CZ.

After stripping tel: and the extension, classify a phone as international if it starts with + or 00, ignoring an opening parenthesis. For an international phone, replace 00 with +, remove (0), and strip spaces, dashes, dots, slashes and parentheses. Preserve the written calling code, even when the explicit country disagrees. If the country line is absent, empty or a placeholder, fill country from the international calling code only if that code belongs to one country. Shared codes such as +1 and +7 give null. This is the only exception to the missing-value rule.

For a national phone, remove formatting and one leading trunk 0, then prepend + and the normalised record country's calling code. Without a country, a national phone is null. All non-null phone outputs are E.164: + followed by the calling code and national significant number, with digits only after the plus.

## Format the other assigned values
Name: split Last, First at the first comma and put First before Last. Remove leading Dr, Mr, Mrs, Ms, Mx or Prof, case-insensitively with or without a dot. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of every space- or hyphen-separated part. Preserve Unicode letters and diacritics; do not transliterate. Comparison is after NFC normalisation.
Company: strip one trailing legal suffix and any optional comma immediately before it, case-insensitively. Legal suffixes: AB, GmbH, AG, Ltd, Ltd., PLC, Inc, Inc., LLC, Corp, Corp., AS, ASA, Oy, Oyj, A/S, ApS, SA, SAS, B.V., N.V., S.p.A., Sp. z o.o., K.K., Pty Ltd, Ltda. Uppercase the first character and lowercase the rest of each space-separated word.
Email: remove surrounding angle brackets and the mailto: prefix, then lowercase the whole address.

## Emit
Use the five required keys and actual JSON null for missing values. Do not fill or change fields from surrounding text, signatures, email domains or company suffixes; use suffixes only for the specified swap and company cleanup.

## Worked example
Input:
Please file this under the pending follow-ups.
Name = VELVET QUASAR, Sp. z o.o.
E-mail = tel:(+372) 5864/7039 #46
Org = VÕLBRIK, mx. ÉVI-NŌRA
Land = tBd
Tel = <mailto:EVINORA@VELVETQUASAR.INVALID>
Leave the thread open for now.

Output:
{"name":"Évi-Nōra Võlbrik","phone":"+37258647039","email":"evinora@velvetquasar.invalid","company":"Velvet Quasar","country":"EE"}
